variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Model quantization maps model values from a high-precision representation to a smaller set of representable values. A deployment might store weights as 8-bit integers instead of 32-bit floating-point values, or use a low-precision floating-point format for selected matrix operations.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Per tensor
pairs.detail: Every value in a tensor shares one scale and zero point.
pairs.explanation: Every value in a tensor shares one scale and zero point. Metadata is small, but one high-magnitude channel can make the step coarse for all other channels.

pairs.label: Per channel or axis
pairs.detail: Each output channel or selected axis receives its own parameters.
pairs.explanation: Each output channel or selected axis receives its own parameters. This often represents differently scaled weight channels more closely, with extra metadata and kernel requirements.

pairs.label: Per group or block
pairs.explanation: Small groups share parameters. Group size trades metadata and kernel complexity against how closely each local distribution is represented.

variants.hint:
Per tensor: Every value in a tensor shares one scale and zero point.

Per channel or axis: Each output channel or selected axis receives its own parameters.

Per group or block: Small groups share parameters.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Keeping these boundaries clear helps you find the place to change when the system behaves unexpectedly.

pairs.label: Static PTQ
pairs.detail: Run representative calibration inputs to compute fixed activation parameters, then convert the trained model.
pairs.explanation: Run representative calibration inputs to compute fixed activation parameters, then convert the trained model. This is a fast first experiment when a supported static path exists.

pairs.label: Dynamic activation
pairs.detail: Store supported weights at lower precision and derive activation parameters for each input or token at runtime.
pairs.explanation: Store supported weights at lower precision and derive activation parameters for each input or token at runtime. This can adapt to changing ranges but adds quantization work to inference.

pairs.label: QAT
pairs.detail: Insert fake-quantization behavior during training or fine-tuning.
pairs.explanation: Insert fake-quantization behavior during training or fine-tuning. Parameters can adapt to rounding and clipping, but training cost and reproducibility become part of the release.
